sights.n: Tamatsukuri Inari Shrine (玉造稲荷神社)
sights.address: Tamatsukuri, Chūō-ku, Osaka (5 min walk from JR Morinomiya / Metro Tamatsukuri exit 1)
sights.w: An ancient shrine on the Uemachi plateau, said to date from 12 BC and long linked to the guardianship of Osaka Castle. OSAKA-INFO calls it the 'princess shrine' because all its deities are goddesses, and it draws women praying for good matches and health. It is also tied to the magatama (curved bead) craft the Tamatsukuri district is named for.

sights.n: Miyuki-mori Tenjingū (御幸森天神宮, Ikuno Koreatown)
sights.w: A shrine at the head of Ikuno Koreatown, said to be founded in 406, where Emperor Nintoku rested on falconry outings ('Miyuki no Mori'). It is registered as one of Osaka City's urban landscape resources, and its 1,600th-anniversary festival was held in 2006.
